MuJoCo / Physics

Try a different world.

Take one moment in a robot's run and see two futures unfold together. Change the ground, gravity or a sideways shove, then scrub to the moment they part ways.

Yours to keep

A reproducible physics experiment and measurements CSV.

Open the harness guide ↗

Start something of your own

Give the agent a direction.

In Harness, start a MuJoCo project and paste this into the agent chat. Change the idea to make it yours.

Continue from something you kept

Keep the result in this project, or give the agent the path to your downloaded copy.

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Catch a moment

    Open What if, choose a body to follow and pin the current state.

  2. Change one thing

    Try Slippery ground or Lunar gravity, then Compare futures. Scrub both worlds together and inspect where they separate.

  3. Keep the experiment

    Save experiment preserves the model, its assets, the starting state, controls and measured frames. Measurements CSV keeps the numbers too.

Both futures use the same recorded controls. This compares open-loop physics; it does not rerun the Python controller.

Blender / 3D design

Shape it until it feels right.

Ask for the controls that matter to your design. Turn them yourself, watch Blender rebuild the geometry, and keep the directions you want to come back to.

Yours to keep

Source, chosen values, model, measurements and a standalone rebuild script.

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Choose your controls

    Ask the agent for meaningful Shape Lab controls in the scene it builds. The starter mug already has a set to try.

  2. Find a direction

    Change the values and build a preview. Orbit the actual geometry, keep a named design and compare it with another.

  3. Make it yours

    Download a kept design's project ZIP. Use values on next build carries your chosen values into the agent's next full export and render.

Each preview builds real Blender geometry. Build time depends on the scene; previews stay separate from the main export until the next full build.

There is another craft to try.Games with Godogen →

Godogen / Games

Try that moment again.

Miss a jump, rewind and try another move. When something feels great or needs work, pin the exact moment so the agent can see what you mean.

Yours to keep

A screenshot, complete game state, feedback and that version's compiled game.

Open the harness guide ↗

Continue from something you kept

Keep the result in this project, or give the agent the path to your downloaded copy.

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Play a little

    Enter Play in a game with Rewind support. The viewer remembers the recent run while you play.

  2. Try another move

    Open Rewind and scrub back. Try from here resumes from that state; returning to the live moment restores the run you left.

  3. Pin what matters

    Pin moment with a Keep, Change or Explore note. Saved moments reopens that game version, screenshot and state after later edits.

Rewind needs snapshot support in the authored game. Saved moments preserve compiled output; editable source stays in the project, and external assets still need their original service.

There is another craft to try.Music with Strudel →

Strudel / Music

Perform the version you love.

A track is an instrument you can play. Bring voices in and out, try a code change and mark the part you want to hear again. Keep the sound of that performance.

Yours to keep

A stereo WAV, played code versions and a timed performance journal in a ZIP.

Continue from something you kept

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Start the instrument

    Click Play, listen to the voices and choose Record take when you are ready.

  2. Perform it

    Mute or solo a voice, run a code change and mark a moment. Finish take opens the captured stereo audio with a seekable waveform.

  3. Keep the sound

    Name the performance and Keep take. Reopen it from Takes or download Audio + source to carry it away.

Takes capture up to two minutes of the instrument's output. The WAV preserves what you heard from it; external samples and custom imports are not bundled.

There is another craft to try.Molecules with RDKit →

RDKit / Molecules

See a molecule turn.

Choose a flexible bond and move through its sampled shapes. Watch atoms approach one another, follow the calculated energy curve and keep a pose worth investigating.

Yours to keep

Input and sampled conformers, selected SDF, energy CSV and reproducible calculation source.

Open the harness guide ↗

Start something of your own

Give the agent a direction.

In Harness, start a RDKit project and paste this into the agent chat. Change the idea to make it yours.

Continue from something you kept

Keep the result in this project, or give the agent the path to your downloaded copy.

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Pick a bond

    Open Bond scan and Use current conformer. Choose a four-atom chain, or measure a dihedral with T and four atom clicks.

  2. Explore its shapes

    Scan bond, then drag the energy curve, scrub the rotation or jump to the lowest sampled point. Compare against the starting pose.

  3. Keep a study

    Choose a pose, add a note and Keep study. Download the full scan and its Python reproducer, or reopen it from the saved library.

This is a rigid MMFF94 scan, with the other internal coordinates fixed. It does not establish a relaxed barrier, equilibrium population or biological activity.

There is another craft to try.Documents with Typst →

Typst / Documents

Point at what you mean.

Hold a draft still while you read it. Quote a sentence, circle a detail or leave a page note, then compare the next draft without losing the one you reviewed.

Yours to keep

The reviewed PDF, anchored notes, readable feedback and a portable review ZIP.

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Hold this draft

    Open Review and Hold this draft. The exact PDF stays still while the agent continues working.

  2. Point and explain

    Select text and Note selected text, Pin an area or add a Page note. Mark it Change, Keep or Question and write what you mean.

  3. Carry it forward

    Keep review, then ask the agent to read its review.md. Compare latest deliberately; unique exact quotations can follow text to another page.

Changed or repeated quotations need human inspection. Area and page notes stay with the reviewed PDF. The packet includes the PDF and feedback; editable source stays in the workspace.

There is another craft to try.Data with Jev Sheets →

Jev Sheets / Data

Ask a better question.

Before asking a whole spreadsheet, compare two versions of a question on frozen rows. Read the answers side by side and use your judgment to decide what the wording missed.

Yours to keep

Frozen rows, exact questions, answers, probabilities, provider details, your notes and CSV/ZIP exports.

Continue from something you kept

Keep the result in this project, or give the agent the path to your downloaded copy.

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Freeze a sample

    Open Question Lab, choose an existing question and write a candidate. Preview 10, 20 or 40 rows and inspect the exact text and context.

  2. Compare the wording

    Compare asks both versions together. Inspect changed answers and full probabilities, then mark Original, New wording or Unsure and add your notes.

  3. Keep your reasoning

    Keep this trial saves the evidence. Try on whole sheet adds the candidate as a separate column; ask the agent to retain the chosen header in sheet.json.

Real answers send sampled rows to your connected Jev provider and require a key. Offline mode is practice only. Confidence and reviewer preferences are not measures of accuracy.

There is another craft to try.Circuits with CircuitJS →

CircuitJS / Circuits

See what changed in the signal.

Capture a circuit, turn a component value and overlay the new trace. Place two cursors around the part that interests you and keep the observations with the circuit that produced them.

Yours to keep

Native circuit exports, timestamped measurements, an SVG plot, notes and a checksummed ZIP.

Continue from something you kept

Keep the result in this project, or give the agent the path to your downloaded copy.

Then get your hands on it

Make a choice. See it happen.

  1. Capture a window

    Open Scope Lab, choose named nodes or component voltage/current, select a duration and Capture circuit.

  2. Compare a change

    Change a component in the circuit and capture again. Choose the earlier take in Compare with; place A and B cursors and zoom between them.

  3. Keep both traces

    Name each take, record what you noticed and Keep capture. Your captures reopens saved traces; Download capture.zip carries the circuit and observations away.

Each capture starts a separate native simulation from the current circuit export. It uses a fresh time origin; initial transients can differ. Keep both captures to preserve a comparison.
